title: vep-rs
description: vep-rs is a fast, memory-efficient variant effect predictor written in Rust. It annotates genomic variants with their predicted functional effects on genes, transcripts, and protein sequences, implementing the Ensembl Variant Effect Predictor (VEP) algorithm, reading a JSON transcript cache built from Ensembl release files or converted from a Perl VEP cache, and producing compatible output. Its concordance with Ensembl VEP release 115.2 is measured at population scale: over 260 million VEP consequence tuples from ClinVar, gnomAD and 1000 Genomes data on GRCh37 and GRCh38, reported per dataset and per Sequence Ontology term, with raw F1 above 0.9999 on each of the six SNP and indel datasets and structural variants measured separately. Wall time is measured against VEP and fastVEP on twenty independently provisioned machines per engine and architecture. Every published aggregate re-derives from the data files released with the code, and the accompanying manuscript documents the remaining divergence classes.
